paragraphs: SIGA Technologies, Inc. is referred to throughout this report as "SIGA," "the Company," "we" or "us."

We are a commercial-stage pharmaceutical company. The Company sells its lead product, TPOXX® ("oral TPOXX®," also known as "tecovirimat," "Tecovirimat-SIGA," or "TEPOXX (tecovirimat)" in certain international markets), to the U.S. Government and international governments (including government affiliated entities). In certain international markets, the Company may sell TPOXX® through a distributor. Additionally, the Company sells the intravenous formulation of TPOXX® ("IV TPOXX®") to the U.S. Government.

TPOXX® is an antiviral drug for the treatment of human smallpox disease caused by variola virus. On July 13, 2018, the United States Food & Drug Administration ("FDA") approved the oral formulation of TPOXX® for the treatment of smallpox. The Company has been delivering oral TPOXX® to the U.S. Strategic National Stockpile ("Strategic Stockpile") since 2013.
On May 18, 2022, the FDA approved IV TPOXX® for the treatment of smallpox.

In addition to being approved by the FDA, oral TPOXX® (tecovirimat) has received regulatory approval from the European Medicines Agency ("EMA"), Health Canada, the Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency ("MHRA") of the United Kingdom, and the Japanese Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency ("PMDA"). The EMA, MHRA and PMDA approved oral TPOXX® for the treatment of smallpox, monkeypox ("mpox"), cowpox, and vaccinia complications following vaccination against smallpox. Health Canada approved TPOXX® for the treatment of smallpox.

TPOXX® was authorized under "exceptional circumstances" by the EMA and the MHRA, under the brand name Tecovirimat-SIGA. These regulators granted marketing authorizations under "exceptional circumstances" because it was not possible to obtain complete efficacy and safety information about the product due to the rarity of smallpox and other orthopoxviruses and because ethical considerations prevented conducting the necessary clinical studies. The Tecovirimat-SIGA marketing authorizations under "exceptional circumstances" are subject to certain specific obligations to gather additional data post-approval to help confirm the product's safety and efficacy. All "exceptional circumstances" marketing authorizations are subject to annual reassessments that consider whether data generated pursuant to the specific obligations continue to confirm its positive benefit-risk profile. These annual reassessments determine whether the product's marketing authorization should be maintained, changed, suspended, or withdrawn based on its benefit-risk profile.

On July 24, 2025, the EMA's Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) closed its third annual reassessment for Tecovirimat-SIGA and initiated a referral procedure for the product following questions over its effectiveness in the treatment of mpox. These questions were raised following receipt of results from certain non-SIGA sponsored clinical trials evaluating tecovirimat as a potential mpox treatment including the PALM007 and STOMP clinical trials. In the referral procedure, CHMP reviewed all available data on the safety and efficacy of Tecovirimat-SIGA for all its authorized indications in order to make a recommendation to the European Commission whether the marketing authorization should be maintained, modified, suspended or withdrawn. The CHMP is expected to meet in March to issue its recommendation. We expect the CHMP will confirm the positive benefit-risk balance of Tecovirimat-SIGA as a treatment for smallpox, cowpox, and vaccinia complications, and maintain those indications in the product label. Regarding mpox, based on the results of the mpox clinical trials, we expect the CHMP will recommend withdrawal of the mpox indication. In the UK, Tecovirimat-SIGA is undergoing an annual reassessment by the MHRA. This reassessment, which is ongoing, is substantially similar to the EMA's annual reassessment process and could result in a similar outcome.
With respect to the regulatory approvals by the EMA, PMDA, MHRA and Health Canada, oral tecovirimat represents the same formulation approved by the FDA in July 2018 under the brand name TPOXX®.

In connection with a potential FDA label expansion of oral TPOXX® for an indication covering smallpox post-exposure prophylaxis ("PEP"), the Company has completed an immunogenicity trial and an expanded safety trial. The timing of a potential submission of a supplemental New Drug Application to the FDA ("Supplemental NDA") for a smallpox PEP indication for oral TPOXX® will be based on the results of ongoing sample analyses from the immunogenicity trial; the Company is currently targeting a Supplemental NDA submission within the next twelve months.

Future macroeconomic volatility, including changes to and uncertainty regarding tariffs and trade policies, could cause cost increases resulting in an adverse effect on the Company's operating results. The Company's supply chain was designed to lessen the impact of macroeconomic volatility such as through development of a U.S. domestic supply chain including U.S. production of API and finished product, and minimal reliance on ex-U.S. components for API and oral TPOXX®.

With respect to IV TPOXX®, tariff activity or other trading restrictions involving the U.S. and Europe may materially increase raw material costs for IV TPOXX® and, in turn, may materially increase IV TPOXX® overall manufacturing costs.

On September 10, 2018, the Company entered into a contract with the U.S. Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority ("BARDA") pursuant to which SIGA agreed to deliver up to 1,488,000 courses of oral TPOXX® to the Strategic Stockpile, and to manufacture and deliver to the Strategic Stockpile, or store as vendor-managed inventory, up to 212,000 courses of IV TPOXX®. In October 2023, the contract was modified so that a course of IV TPOXX® was redefined within the contract from being 14 vials to being 28 vials; as such, the 19C BARDA Contract currently specifies 106,000 courses of IV TPOXX® (for the same payment amount as originally specified). In addition to the delivery of TPOXX® courses, the contract includes funding from BARDA for a range of activities, including advanced development of IV TPOXX®, post-marketing activities for oral and IV TPOXX®, development of a pediatric formulation, support for manufacturing activities, and procurement activities. On April 8, 2025, total payments contemplated under the contract with BARDA were increased by $14.3 million to add funding for activities supporting manufacturing. On June 3, 2025, total payments contemplated under the contract with BARDA were increased by $13.2 million in connection with the development of the pediatric formulation of TPOXX®. As of December 31, 2025, the contract with BARDA (as amended, modified, or supplemented from time to time, the "19C BARDA Contract") contemplates up to approximately $630 million of payments, of which approximately $79.2 million of payments are included within the base period of performance, approximately $545.2 million of payments are related to exercised options and up to approximately $5.6 million of payments are currently specified as unexercised options. BARDA may choose in its sole discretion when, or whether, to exercise any of the unexercised options. The period of performance for options is up to ten years from the date of entry into the 19C BARDA Contract and such options could be exercised at any time during the contract term.

The base period of performance specifies potential payments of approximately $79.2 million for the following activities: payments of approximately $11.1 million for the delivery of approximately 35,700 courses of oral TPOXX® to the Strategic Stockpile; payments of $8.0 million for the manufacture of 10,000 courses (as currently defined within the contract as being 28 vials) of final drug product of IV TPOXX® ("IV FDP"), of which $3.2 million of payments are related to the manufacture of bulk drug substance ("IV BDS") to be used in the manufacture of IV FDP; payments of approximately $59.5 million to fund reimbursed activities; and payments of approximately $0.6 million for supportive procurement activities. As of December 31, 2025, the Company had received $11.1 million for the delivery of approximately 35,700 courses of oral TPOXX® to the Strategic Stockpile, $3.2 million for the manufacture of IV BDS, $4.8 million for the delivery of IV FDP to the Strategic Stockpile, and $31.2 million for other base period activities. IV BDS has been used for the manufacture of courses of IV FDP.

The options that have been exercised as of December 31, 2025, provide for payments up to approximately $545.2 million. As of December 31, 2025, there are exercised options for the following activities: payments up to $450.2 million for the manufacture and delivery of up to 1.5 million courses of oral TPOXX®; payments up to $76.8 million for the manufacture of courses of IV FDP; payments of up to approximately $3.6 million to fund post-marketing activities for IV TPOXX®; and payments of up to $14.6 million for funding of post-marketing activities for oral TPOXX®. As of December 31, 2025, a cumulative total of $450.2 million of oral TPOXX® has been delivered to the Strategic Stockpile and accepted; a cumulative total of $61.4 million of IV BDS or IV FDP has been either set aside in inventory or delivered to the Strategic Stockpile and accepted (IV BDS that has been set aside has been recorded as deferred revenue and will be recognized as revenue when the IV BDS is manufactured as IV FDP and delivered); and the Company has been cumulatively reimbursed $10.9 million in connection with post-marketing activities for oral and IV TPOXX®.

headings: Risks Related to Our Dependence on Government Contracts
Laws and regulations affecting government contracts and grants might make it more costly and difficult for us to successfully conduct our business.
Unfavorable provisions in government contracts and grants, some of which may be customary, may harm our future business, financial condition and potential operating results.
A U.S. Government shutdown could materially adversely affect our business, results of operations, and financial condition.
Our business could be adversely affected by a negative audit by the U.S. Government.
Risks Related to Regulatory Approvals

Failure to obtain regulatory approval for new formulations of TPOXX® in the U.S. would prevent us from commercializing TPOXX® in other than the oral and intravenous formulations for smallpox treatment.

Failure to maintain existing regulatory approvals or obtain future regulatory approvals in additional international jurisdictions could prevent us from marketing our products in certain jurisdictions abroad.
Risks Related to Commercial and International Activities

We reacquired international promotional rights and we may be unable successfully to expand our internal international sales and marketing capabilities or enter into agreements with third parties outside of the U.S.
We are subject to complex and changing laws and regulations worldwide, which exposes us to potential liability, increased cost, and other adverse effects on our business.
We have incurred in the past, and could incur net losses in the future, including if we fail to enter into a new procurement contract with the U.S. Government.
Risks Related to Manufacturing, Storage and Our Dependence on Third Parties

If third parties on whom we rely for packaging and delivery of our products, are unable to meet the target timing for deliveries to our customers, product revenue recognition may be delayed and our business could suffer.
Problems related to large-scale commercial manufacturing could cause an increase in costs or shortages of products or a delay in product launches.
Risks Related to Product Development
Liquid Suspension/Pediatric TPOXX® formulations are currently in product development and there can be no assurance of successful development or ultimate commercialization.
Risks Related to Our Intellectual Property
Our ability to compete may decrease if we do not adequately protect our intellectual property rights.
Risks Related to Our Common Stock

Affiliates of MacAndrews & Forbes Incorporated (together with its affiliates "MacAndrews") have substantial ownership of SIGA stock and their interests may differ from the interests of other stockholders.
A future issuance of preferred stock may adversely affect the rights of the holders of our common stock.
General Risk Factors
Global infectious disease outbreaks, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, or climate-related matters could negatively impact the global economy on a broad scale and our business in particular.
The health security markets in which we compete and will compete are highly competitive.
Product liability lawsuits could cause us to incur liabilities, which could be substantial, and require us to limit commercialization of any products that we may develop.
Our activities may involve hazardous materials, use of which may subject us to environmental regulatory liabilities.
paragraphs: This report contains forward-looking statements and other prospective information relating to future events. These forward-looking statements and other information are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from our historical results or currently anticipated results, including the following:

We expect a substantial percentage of our future operating revenues to come from contracts with the U.S. Government for the provision and maintenance of the stockpile of TPOXX® built under the 19C BARDA Contract. If the U.S. Government does not enter into such a contract, or if such contract is materially delayed or smaller than the 19C BARDA Contract, our long-term business, financial condition and operating results could be materially harmed.

The success of our business and our operating results for the foreseeable future will be substantially dependent on the U.S. Government's commitment to maintaining or expanding its stockpile of TPOXX®. Failure to secure in a timely manner and perform additional U.S. Government contracts after the 19C BARDA Contract to substantially maintain or expand the U.S. Government stockpile of TPOXX® could have a material adverse effect on our long-term business, financial condition, results of operations, including losses due to potential inventory write-offs, and prospects. Additionally, the 19C BARDA Contract does not necessarily increase the likelihood that we will secure future comparable contracts with the U.S. Government.

Government contracts require ongoing funding decisions by governments. A substantial percentage of our potential future revenues are expected to come from government contracts. The majority of potential revenue under any future U.S. Government contract will likely be tied to options that may or may not be exercised at the sole discretion of the U.S. Government. Failure of the U.S. Government to exercise its options under a new procurement contract to supply TPOXX® to the U.S. Government could cause our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects to be materially harmed.

Government-funded contracts often consist of standalone procurement orders or a base period of performance followed by options for the performance of certain future activities. The value of goods and services subject to options may constitute the majority of the total value of the underlying contract, as in the case of the 19C BARDA Contract as well as any new contract to continue supplying TPOXX® to the U.S. Government.

The funding of government programs, which fund BARDA's purchases under the 19C BARDA Contract and are expected to fund any new contract to supply TPOXX® to the U.S. Government, is subject to Congressional appropriations, generally made on a fiscal year basis even though a program may continue for several years. Our government customers are subject to political considerations and budgetary constraints, which result in uncertainties as to continued funding of their ongoing programs, including SIGA's contracts.

paragraphs: SIGA Technologies, Inc. 會在本報告中被稱為 "SIGA," "the Company," "we" 或 "us."

本公司為一家商業階段的製藥公司。本公司銷售其主要產品 TPOXX® ("口服 TPOXX®," 也稱為 "tecovirimat," "Tecovirimat-SIGA," 或 "TEPOXX (tecovirimat)" 在某些國際市場)，至美國政府與國際政府（包括政府附屬機構）。在某些國際市場，本公司可能透過經銷商銷售 TPOXX®。此外，本公司也銷售 TPOXX® 的靜脈注射製劑（"IV TPOXX®"）至美國政府。
TPOXX® 是一種抗病毒藥物，用於治療由 variola 病毒引起的人類天花疾病。2018 年 7 月 13 日，美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）批准口服 TPOXX® 用於治療天花。本公司自 2013 年起已開始向美國國家戰略儲備庫（"Strategic Stockpile"）供應口服 TPOXX®。
2022 年 5 月 18 日，FDA 批准 IV TPOXX® 用於治療天花。

除了獲得 FDA 批准外，口服 TPOXX® (tecovirimat) 也獲得歐洲藥物管理局（"EMA"）、加拿大衛生部、英國藥物及醫療產品規管局（"MHRA"）以及日本 Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency（"PMDA"）的藥物許可。EMA、MHRA 和 PMDA 批准口服 TPOXX® 用於治療天花、猴痘（"mpox"）、牛痘以及接種天花疫苗後的 vaccinia 並發症。加拿大衛生部批准 TPOXX® 用於治療天花。

TPOXX® 在 EMA 和 MHRA 的 "exceptional circumstances" 下獲得授權，品牌為 Tecovirimat-SIGA。這些監管機構在 "exceptional circumstances" 下授予市場許可，因為無法取得完整的效果與安全性資料，這是因為天花及其他正痘病毒的罕見性，以及倫理考量使進行必要的臨牀試驗變得不可能。Tecovirimat-SIGA 在 "exceptional circumstances" 下的市場許可，需遵守某些特定義務，以收集更多資料以確認產品的安全性與有效性。所有 "exceptional circumstances" 的市場許可均需每年重新評估，以考量根據特定義務產生的資料是否持續確認其正面的效益與風險平衡。這些年度評估將決定產品的市場許可是否應維持、修改、暫停或撤回，根據其效益與風險平衡。

2025 年 7 月 24 日，EMA 的人用藥品委員會（CHMP）完成 Tecovirimat-SIGA 的第三年度評估，並因對其治療 mpox 的有效性產生疑問而啟動產品轉交程序。這些疑問是因收到某些非 SIGA 資助的臨牀試驗結果而產生，這些試驗評估 tecovirimat 作為 mpox 治療的潛力，包括 PALM007 和 STOMP 臨牀試驗。在轉交程序中，CHMP 評估所有 Tecovirimat-SIGA 的安全性與有效性資料，以針對其所有核准適應症做出建議，是否應維持、修改、暫停或撤回市場許可。CHMP 預計於 3 月會議中發佈建議。我們預期 CHMP 將確認 Tecovirimat-SIGA 作為治療天花、牛痘以及 vaccinia 並發症的正面效益與風險平衡，並維持這些適應症在產品說明書中。關於 mpox，根據 mpox 臨牀試驗的結果，我們預期 CHMP 將建議撤回 mpox 的適應症。在英國，Tecovirimat-SIGA 正在由 MHRA 進行年度評估。此評估持續進行中，與 EMA 的年度評估程序類似，可能導致類似的結果。
關於 EMA、PMDA、MHRA 和加拿大衛生部的藥物核准，口服 tecovirimat 代表與 FDA 在 2018 年 7 月核准的相同製劑，品牌為 TPOXX®。
為因應美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）可能對口服 TPOXX® 製劑標籤擴張，用於小兒麻痺症後暴露預防（"PEP"）的適應症，本公司已完成免疫原性試驗與擴展安全性試驗。潛在提交補充新藥申請（"Supplemental NDA"）至 FDA 的時間點，將根據免疫原性試驗中持續進行樣本分析的結果而定；本公司目前目標是在未來十二個月內提交 Supplemental NDA。
未來總體經濟波動，包括關稅與貿易政策的變動與不確定性，可能導致成本增加，進而對本公司營運成果產生不利影響。本公司供應鏈設計旨在降低總體經濟波動的影響，例如透過發展美國本土供應鏈，包括美國生產活性藥物成分（API）與成品，以及對 API 與口服 TPOXX® 的外來美國零組件依賴程度極低。
關於 IV TPOXX®，美國與歐洲之間的關稅活動或其他貿易限制，可能顯著提高 IV TPOXX® 原料成本，進而可能顯著提高 IV TPOXX® 的整體製造成本。

於 2018 年 9 月 10 日，本公司與美國生物先進研究與開發管理局（"BARDA"）簽訂契約，SIGA 同意交付最多 1,488,000 份口服 TPOXX® 給戰略儲備庫，並製造與交付至戰略儲備庫，或作為供應商管理存貨，最多 212,000 份 IV TPOXX®。於 2023 年 10 月，契約被修改，將 IV TPOXX® 一課程重新定義為 28 支而非原來的 14 支；因此，目前的 19C BARDA 契約規範 106,000 份 IV TPOXX®（與原來指定的付款金額相同）。除了 TPOXX® 課程的交付，契約還包含 BARDA 對一系列活動的資金支持，包括 IV TPOXX® 的先進開發、口服與 IV TPOXX® 的上市後活動、兒童用製劑的開發、製造活動的支持，以及採購活動。於 2025 年 4 月 8 日，與 BARDA 契約預期的總付款額增加 14.3 百萬美元，以增加製造活動支持的資金。於 2025 年 6 月 3 日，與 BARDA 契約預期的總付款額再增加 13.2 百萬美元，用以支持 TPOXX® 兒童用製劑的開發。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，與 BARDA 契約（包括隨時間變動的修正、修改或補充，稱為 "19C BARDA 契約"）預期的總付款額約為 630 百萬美元，其中約 79.2 百萬美元的付款包含在契約基本履行期間內，約 545.2 百萬美元的付款與已行使的選擇權有關，而目前約 5.6 百萬美元的付款則為尚未行使的選擇權。BARDA 可以自行決定是否以及何時行使任何尚未行使的選擇權。選擇權的履行期間為自 19C BARDA 契約簽訂日起最多十年，且選擇權可在契約期間內任何時間行使。

基本履行期間的付款規範約為 79.2 百萬美元，用於以下活動：約 11.1 百萬美元用於交付約 35,700 份口服 TPOXX® 給戰略儲備庫；8.0 百萬美元用於製造 10,000 份（根據契約目前定義為 28 支）IV TPOXX® 最終藥品製劑（"IV FDP"），其中 3.2 百萬美元用於製造 IV TPOXX® 的活性藥物成分（"IV BDS"）以供製造 IV FDP；約 59.5 百萬美元用於資助可報銷活動；以及約 0.6 百萬美元用於支持採購活動。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司已收到 11.1 百萬美元用於交付約 35,700 份口服 TPOXX® 給戰略儲備庫，3.2 百萬美元用於製造 IV BDS，4.8 百萬美元用於交付 IV FDP 給戰略儲備庫，以及 31.2 百萬美元用於其他基本履行期間活動。IV BDS 已用於製造 IV FDP 課程。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，已行使的選擇權提供約 545.2 百萬美元的付款。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，已行使的選擇權包括以下活動：最多 450.2 百萬美元用於製造與交付最多 150 萬份口服 TPOXX®；最多 76.8 百萬美元用於製造 IV FDP 課程；最多約 3.6 百萬美元用於資助 IV TPOXX® 的上市後活動；以及最多 14.6 百萬美元用於資助口服 TPOXX® 的上市後活動。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，已累計交付 450.2 百萬美元的口服 TPOXX® 給戰略儲備庫並被接受；已累計將 61.4 百萬美元的 IV BDS 或 IV FDP 保留為存貨或交付至戰略儲備庫並被接受（已保留的 IV BDS 已記錄為遞延收入，並將在 IV BDS 製造為 IV FDP 並交付時確認為收入）；且本公司已累計因口服與 IV TPOXX® 的上市後活動而獲得 10.9 百萬美元的補償。

TPOXX® 為用以治療由 variola 病毒引起之人類天花疾病之抗病毒藥物。2018 年 7 月 13 日，美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）批准口服 TPOXX® 用以治療天花。本公司自 2013 年起已將口服 TPOXX® 配送至美國國家戰略儲備（"Strategic Stockpile"）。

headings: 與我們對政府契約依賴相關的風險
影響政府契約及補助金的法律與法規可能會使我們成功經營業務的成本與困難度增加。
政府契約及補助金中不利的條款，其中一些可能是慣例，可能會對我們未來的業務、財務狀況及潛在營運成果造成損害。
美國政府停擺可能會對我們的業務、營運成果及財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
我們的業務可能因美國政府的負面審計而受到不利影響。
與監管許可相關的風險
未能取得美國對 TPOXX® 新配方的監管許可將會阻止我們在小pox治療方面除口服及靜脈注射配方以外的其他配方商業化。
未能維持現有監管許可或取得未來在其他國際司法管轄區的監管許可可能會阻止我們在某些海外司法管轄區推廣我們的產品。
與商業及國際業務相關的風險
我們重新取得國際推廣權，我們可能無法成功擴展我們的內部國際銷售與行銷能力，或與美國境外的第三方簽訂協議。
我們面臨全球複雜且不斷變化的法律與法規，這使我們面臨潛在的責任、增加的成本，以及其他對我們業務的不利影響。
我們過去曾產生過虧損，未來也可能產生淨虧損，包括我們未能與美國政府簽訂新的採購合約的情況。
與製造、儲存及我們對第三方依賴相關的風險
若我們依賴的第三方無法按時完成產品包裝與配送，產品收入認列可能延遲，導致我們的業務受損。
與大規模商業製造相關的問題可能導致成本增加、產品短缺或產品發佈延遲。
與產品開發相關的風險
液態懸浮劑/兒童用 TPOXX® 製劑目前處於產品開發階段，無法保證能成功開發或最終實現商業化。
與我們智慧財產權相關的風險
若我們未能充分保護智慧財產權，可能影響我們的競爭能力。
與我們普通股相關的風險
MacAndrews & Forbes Incorporated 的關係企業（與其關係企業合稱 "MacAndrews"）持有大量 SIGA 股票，其利益可能與其他股東的利益不同。
未來發行優先股可能不利於我們普通股持有人之權利。
一般風險因素
全球傳染病爆發，例如 COVID-19 疫情，或與氣候相關的議題，可能對全球經濟造成廣泛影響，並特別影響我們的業務。
我們所競爭且將繼續競爭的健康安全市場為高度競爭性市場。
產品責任訴訟可能導致我們產生重大負債，並可能要求我們限制任何可能開發產品的商業化。
我們的業務活動可能涉及危險物料，其使用可能使我們面臨環境法規相關的負債。
paragraphs: 本報告包含有關未來事件的預測性陳述及其他前瞻性資訊。這些預測性陳述及其他資訊受到風險與不確定性影響，可能導致我們的實際結果與歷史結果或目前預期結果有重大差異，包括以下內容：
我們預期未來營運收入的相當大比例將來自與美國政府簽訂的合同，用以提供及維護根據19C BARDA合同所建置的TPOXX®儲備。若美國政府未簽訂此類合同，或該合同有重大延遲或規模小於19C BARDA合同，將可能對我們的長期營運、財務狀況及營運結果造成重大損害。
我們業務的成功及未來一段時間的營運結果將大幅依賴美國政府維持或擴充TPOXX®儲備的承諾。若在19C BARDA合同到期後未能及時取得並執行其他美國政府合同，以大幅維持或擴充美國政府的TPOXX®儲備，將可能對我們的長期營運、財務狀況、營運結果，包括潛在存貨減損所導致的損失，以及前景造成重大不利影響。此外，19C BARDA合同並不一定會增加我們取得未來類似美國政府合同的機率。
政府合同需要政府持續進行經費決策。我們潛在未來收入的相當大比例預期將來自政府合同。任何未來美國政府合同下的潛在收入，很可能與美國政府單方面決定是否執行的選項掛鉤。若美國政府未執行新採購合同下供應TPOXX®給美國政府的選項，將可能對我們的營運、財務狀況、營運結果及前景造成重大損害。
政府資助的合同通常包含獨立採購訂單，或為基礎執行期後接續某些未來活動的選項。選項所涉及的商品與服務價值，可能構成基礎合同總價值的絕大部分，如19C BARDA合同以及任何新合同用以持續供應TPOXX®給美國政府的情況亦然。
資助BARDA根據19C BARDA合同所進行採購的政府計畫，以及預期資助任何新合同用以供應TPOXX®給美國政府的計畫，其經費取得取決於國會的撥款，通常以財政年度為單位進行，即使計畫可能持續數年。我們的政府客戶受到政治考量與預算限制的影響，導致其持續經費的不確定性，包括SIGA的合同。
